title: ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON THE EMPLOYMENT IMPROVEMENT OF DOMESTIC WORKERS
title_original: 가사근로자의 고용개선 등에 관한 법률 시행령

ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE ACT ON THE EMPLOYMENT IMPROVEMENT OF DOMESTIC WORKERS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters mandated by the Act on the Employment Improvement of Domestic Workers and matters necessary for the enforcement thereof.

Article 2 (Requirements for certification of domestic service providers) (1) "Standards prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as the number of workers hired" in Article 7(1)2 of the Act on the Employment Improvement of Domestic Workers (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") means the following:
  1. At least 5 domestic workers shall be regularly employed, or their regular employment shall be planned;
  2. Domestic workers (excluding those who are not eligible under the relevant statutes) shall be covered by all the following insurance and pension plans:
  a. Employment insurance and industrial accident compensation insurance under the Act on the Collection of Insurance Premiums for Employment Insurance and Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance;
  b. National health insurance under the National Health Insurance Act;
  c. National pension under the National Pension Act;
  3. Domestic workers shall be paid wages equal to or higher than the minimum wage under Article 5 of the Minimum Wage Act.
  (2) "Requirements prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 7 (1) 5 of the Act means the following: <Amended on Dec. 31, 2024>
  1. At least 1 manager shall be appointed in addition to the representative, provided, if the number of domestic workers is less than 50 and the representative concurrently serves as a manager, a manager may not be appointed separately;
  2. At least 50 million won in paid-in capital shall be secured; provided, this requirement shall not apply to non-profit corporations;
  3. The provider shall have an office with an exclusive-use floor area of at least 10 square meters for operating the domestic service provider; provided, where he or she is engaged in fee-charging job placement services under the Employment Security Act and meets the office requirements under the relevant statutes or regulations, he or she shall be deemed to meet the office requirements for a domestic service provider;
  4. Where domestic services are being provided under other statutes, such as the Employment Security Act, the provision of domestic services in the capacity of a domestic service provider shall be operated separately from those services.

Article 3 (Criminal history inquiry) (1) If a domestic service provider requests a criminal history inquiry pursuant to the main clause of Article 13(1) of the Act, it shall submit a written request for a criminal history inquiry to the commissioner of a City/Do police agency or the chief of a police station having jurisdiction over its principal place of business, along with the following documents, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Employment and Labor:
  1. A copy of the certificate of the domestic service provider;
  2. Written consent of the persons subject to criminal history inquiry.
  (2) If a person who intends to become a domestic worker providing protection and nurturing services for children 12 years of age or younger requests a criminal history inquiry to directly submit a written reply to a criminal history inquiry to a domestic service provider pursuant to the proviso of Article 13(1) of the Act, he or she shall submit a written request for a criminal history inquiry to the commissioner of a City/Do police agency or the chief of a police station, along with the following documents, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Employment and Labor; in such cases, if the commissioner of the City/Do police agency or the chief of the police station can verify the information on the documents referred to in subparagraph 1 through joint use of administrative information under Article 36(1) of the Electronic Government Act, the submission of documents may be replaced with such verification:
  1. Documents verifying the identity of the person;
  2. Certificate from a domestic service provider.
  (3) If the commissioner of a City/Do police agency or the chief of a police station, upon receiving a request for a criminal history inquiry under paragraph (1) or (2), provides notification under Article 13(3) of the Act, he or she shall issue a written reply to the criminal history inquiry, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Employment and Labor.

Article 4 (Terms and conditions of employment to be specified at time of conclusion of employment contract) "Matters regarding working conditions prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 14(1)5 of the Act means the following:
  1. Day of the week or date on which domestic services are available;
  2. Hours during which domestic services are available;
  3. Areas where domestic services are available.

Article 5 (Delivery of documents upon request of domestic workers) "Are changed due to reasons prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as a change in the relevant collective agreement or employment rules" in the proviso of Article 14(2) of the Act means any of the following cases:
  1. Where paid holidays are replaced with specific working days by agreement in writing with the workers' representative (referring to the relevant labor union where there is a labor union organized by a majority of workers; and where there is no such union, referring to the person who represents a majority of workers; hereinafter the same shall apply) under the proviso of subparagraph 1 (c) of Appendix 1;
  2. Cases falling under any subparagraph of Article 8-2 of the Enforcement Decree of the Labor Standards Act.

Article 6 (In cases of unavoidable business circumstances) "In cases of unavoidable business circumstances prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso of Article 15(1) of the Act means any of the following cases:
  1. Sales in the month immediately preceding the month which includes the date for which the minimum working hours are to be determined to be less than 15 hours per week (hereafter in this Article referred to as the "base month") decline at least 30/100 compared with the sales falling under any of the following items:
  a. Sales in the same month of the year immediately preceding the year that includes the base month;
  b. Average monthly sales for the three months immediately preceding the base month;
  c. Average monthly sales of the year immediately preceding the year that includes the base month;
  2. Where the sales of the base month and the monthly average sales for each of the 2 quarters immediately preceding the base month successively decline by at least 20/100 each, so that sales show a downward trend.

Article 7 (Paid holidays and annual paid leave) The detailed calculation standards for paid holidays and annual paid leave under Article 16(2) of the Act, and the standards for calculating the wages that the employer of a domestic service provider (hereinafter referred to as the "employer") is required to pay to domestic workers during paid holidays and periods of annual paid leave shall be as specified in Appendix 1.

Article 8 (Subsidization of employment insurance premiums) The Minister of Employment and Labor shall publicly notify matters necessary for, among other things, the specific eligibility for, the level and period of, methods and procedures for, subsidization under Article 18(2) of the Act, considering the level of remuneration for domestic workers, their acquisition of insured status, etc. in consultation with the Minister of Health and Welfare.

Article 9 (Delegation of authority) The Minister of Employment and Labor shall delegate his or her authority over the following matters to the head of a regional employment and labor office pursuant to Article 24(1) of the Act:
  1. Certification of domestic service providers, receipt of applications for certification, certification examination, notification and disclosure of certification results, certification of changes, and receipt of reports on changes under Article 7 of the Act;
  2. Receipt of reports on business suspension or closure or resumption under Article 10 of the Act;
  3. Request for submission of information subject to disclosure under Article 19(2) of the Act;
  4. Entry, inspection, and questioning, and issuance of orders to report or submit data, under Article 22 of the Act;
  5. Issuance of corrective orders, revocation of certification, granting of period to replace representatives or executive officers, and holding of hearings under Article 23 of the Act;
  6. Imposition and collection of administrative fines under Article 28 of the Act (excluding the imposition and collection of administrative fines under paragraph (2)3 of that Article).

Article 10 (Entrustment of affairs) (1) "Tasks prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 24(2)3 of the Act means subsidizing employment insurance premiums and pension premiums under Article 18(2) of the Act.
  (2) Pursuant to Article 24(2) of the Act, the Minister of Employment and Labor shall entrust the affairs referred to in paragraph (1) in accordance with the following classifications:
  1. Subsidization of employment insurance premiums: Entrusted to the Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service under Article 10 of the Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance Act;
  2. Subsidization of pension premiums: Entrusted to the National Pension Service under Article 24 of the National Pension Act.
  (3) Pursuant to Article 24(2) of the Act, the Minister of Employment and Labor shall entrust the establishment and operation of the computerized system under Article 19(1) of the Act to the Korea Employment Information Service under Article 18 of the Framework Act on Employment Policy.
  (4) Pursuant to Article 24(2) of the Act, the Minister of Employment and Labor may entrust affairs relating to fact-finding surveys under Article 21(1) of the Act to the following specialized institutions or organizations:
  1. Government-funded research institutes under the Act on the Establishment, Operation and Fostering of Government-Funded Research Institutes;
  2. Private research institutes (limited to non-profit corporations under Article 32 of the Civil Act);
  3. Other institutions or organizations deemed by the Minister of Employment and Labor to have the human and physical capabilities to perform the entrusted affairs.
  (5) If the Minister of Employment and Labor entrusts affairs pursuant to paragraph (4), he or she shall publicly notify the institution to which the affairs are entrusted and the details of the entrusted affairs.

Article 11 (Processing of sensitive information and personally identifiable information) The Minister of Employment and Labor (including persons to whom the authority or affairs of the Minister of Employment and Labor are delegated or entrusted) may process information on health under Article 23 of the Personal Information Protection Act (limited to the affairs referred to in subparagraph 3), information constituting criminal history records under subparagraph 2 of Article 18 of the Enforcement Decree of that Act (limited to the affairs referred to in subparagraphs 2 and 3), and data containing resident registration numbers or alien registration numbers under subparagraph 1 or 4 of Article 19 of that Enforcement Decree, where unavoidable to perform the following affairs:
  1. Certification, certification of changes, and reporting on changes, of domestic service providers under Article 7 of the Act;
  2. Verification of grounds for disqualification under Article 8 of the Act;
  3. Verification of grounds for disqualification under Article 12 of the Act;
  4. Subsidization of the following insurance premiums under Article 18(2) of the Act:
  a. Employment insurance and industrial accident compensation insurance premiums under the Act on the Collection of Insurance Premiums for Employment Insurance and Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance;
  b. Insurance contributions under the National Health Insurance Act;
  c. Pension premiums under the National Pension Act.

Article 12 (Standards for imposition of administrative fines) The standards for imposing administrative fines under Article 28(1) and (2) of the Act shall be as specified in Appendix 2.

ADDENDUM <Presidential Decree No. 32659, May 31, 2022>
This Decree shall enter into force on June 16, 2022.

ADDENDUM (Presidential Decree on Partial Amendments to 12 Statutes and Regulations to Clarify Capital Standards) <Presidential Decree No. 35172, Dec. 31, 2024>
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

[Appendix 1 | 000100E]
■ Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Employment Improvement of Domestic Workers [Appendix 1]

Detailed Calculation Standards for Paid Holidays and Annual Paid Leave, etc. (Related to Article 7)

1. The detailed calculation standards for paid holidays and the standards for calculating the wages for such holidays shall be as prescribed in the following items:

  (a) The employer shall guarantee domestic workers at least 1 paid holiday per week on average.

  (b) The paid holiday under item (a) shall be granted to a domestic worker who has actually worked the scheduled service hours for 1 week. "Scheduled service hours" means the domestic service hours under the contract for use notified to the domestic worker by the employer pursuant to Article 11 (3) of the Act, excluding hours that do not conform to the working conditions specified in the employment contract pursuant to Article 14 of the Act; hereinafter the same shall apply.

  (c) The employer shall guarantee as paid holidays the public holidays specified in the subparagraphs of Article 2 of the Regulations on Public Holidays of Government Offices (excluding subparagraph 1), and the substitute public holidays under Article 3 of those Regulations: Provided, That, where agreed in writing with the workers' representative, such holidays may be replaced with specified working days.

  (d) The wages that the employer is required to pay to a domestic worker for a paid holiday shall be the daily wage calculated by multiplying the number of hours calculated using the formula in item (e) by the hourly wage. In this case, if the calculated number of hours is less than 1 hour, it shall be rounded up to 1 hour.

  (e) Formula

    [Average actual weekly working hours over 4 weeks (or over the period worked, if less than 4 weeks) ÷ 40 hours] × 8 hours

2. The detailed calculation standards for annual paid leave and the standards for calculating the wages for such leave shall be as prescribed in the following items:

  (a) The employer shall grant 15 days of paid leave to a domestic worker whose actual hours worked during 1 year are at least 80 percent of the annual scheduled service hours.

  (b) The employer shall grant 1 day of paid leave to a domestic worker whose period of continuous service is less than 1 year, or whose actual hours worked during 1 year are less than 80 percent of the annual scheduled service hours, if that worker has actually worked the scheduled service hours for 1 month.

  (c) For a domestic worker who has worked continuously for at least 3 years, the employer shall grant paid leave by adding 1 day for every 2 years of continuous service beyond the initial 1 year to the number of days of paid leave under item (a). In this case, the total number of days of paid leave, including additional leave, shall not exceed 25 days.

  (d) Annual paid leave shall be granted in hours calculated using the formula in item (e), based on the number of days of annual paid leave under items (a) through (c). In this case, a fraction of less than 1 hour shall be rounded up to 1 hour.

  (e) Formula

    Number of days of annual paid leave × (Average actual weekly working hours ÷ 40 hours) × 8 hours

  (f) The average actual weekly working hours in item (e) shall be the hours obtained by dividing the annual actual working hours by the number of weeks in that period in the case of annual paid leave under item (a), and the hours obtained by dividing the actual working hours during 1 month by the number of weeks in that period in the case of annual paid leave under item (b).

  (g) The wages that the employer is required to pay to a domestic worker for annual paid leave shall be calculated by multiplying the number of hours calculated under item (d) by the hourly wage.

[Appendix 2 | 000200E]
■ Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Employment Improvement of Domestic Workers [Appendix 2]

Standards for Imposition of Administrative Fines (Related to Article 12)

1. General standards

  (a) The aggravated standards for imposing administrative fines according to the number of violations shall apply where an administrative fine has been imposed for the same violation within the most recent 1 year. In this case, the period shall be calculated on the basis of the date on which an administrative fine was imposed for the violation and the date on which another commission of the same violation after that disposition was detected.

  (b) When an aggravated disposition is imposed under item (a), the applicable violation tier shall be the tier following the tier of the disposition imposed before that violation (the highest tier, if 2 or more administrative fines were imposed within the period specified in item (a)).

  (c) The imposing authority may reduce an administrative fine under the individual standards in subparagraph 2 by up to one-half in any of the following cases: Provided, That this shall not apply to a violator who is in arrears with an administrative fine.
    1) Where the violation is found to have resulted from minor carelessness or error;
    2) Where the violator is found to have made efforts to rectify or eliminate the state of violation of law;
    3) Where there are circumstances such as the violator having suffered a significant loss of property due to a natural disaster, fire, etc., or the business being in a serious crisis due to deterioration of business conditions;
    4) Where it is otherwise deemed necessary to reduce the amount of the administrative fine in consideration of the degree of the violation, its motive and consequences, etc.
